static_traits.name: Li Na
static_traits.family_status: The father is a missionary, with a 3-year-old child
static_traits.social_status: Relationships with colleagues strained by persistent worry about student performance
static_traits.medical_history: No major physical illness history, no prior psychotherapy history; recently experiencing sleep problems due to work pressure
static_traits.language_features: Clear expression, able to describe trigger situations and impacts specifically; emotional tone rather negative, often using catastrophizing and 'all-or-nothing' expressions; fairly cooperative, able to set small goals together with the counselor

basic_info.main_problem: I have been distressed by the thought that 'my students perform poorly in my class and will ultimately fail'. This belief causes me great pain and also affects my teaching ability.
basic_info.core_demands: Ideally, I want to regain confidence at work, no longer constantly worrying about losing my job or making mistakes.
growth_experiences: At the start of the school year, Li Na noticed some students struggling with certain concepts in learning, giving rise to the thought that 'students perform poorly in my class and will ultimately fail'. These thoughts appear daily during classroom teaching and lesson preparation, intensifying week by week; although she tried implementing new teaching strategies and providing extra support for students, the thoughts persist.

About a month ago, her supervisor joked that she 'types with one hand', triggering intense shame and a sense of being negated. Since then she has persistently worried at work about being seen as incompetent, fearing mistakes and avoiding contact with colleagues and her supervisor; sleep disturbance, irregular eating, persistent tension and decreased attention have appeared, worsening especially during team meetings or when her supervisor reviews her work.
Background and present: father is a missionary; currently married with a 3-year-old child, with fairly high spousal support.

core_beliefs: Students' success or failure depends entirely on me; if they fail it means I fail

special_situations.event: After the new school year began, finding some students struggling with key concepts
special_situations.conditional_assumptions: If any student cannot keep up with my teaching, it means I am a failure as a teacher
special_situations.compensatory_strategies: Working overtime to prepare lessons, implementing new teaching strategies and providing extra support, while constantly worrying about student performance
special_situations.automatic_thoughts: They will never learn well, they will all fail in the end; I am failing

special_situations.event: Repeatedly focusing on problems in student homework and assessments during class and lesson preparation
special_situations.conditional_assumptions: If I cannot eliminate all problems, the final outcome will be terrible
special_situations.compensatory_strategies: Over-monitors and repeatedly checks teaching details, tries to use more methods to 'correct everything'
special_situations.automatic_thoughts: No matter what I do, they will fail in the end

special_situations.event: Interacting with the supervisor (e.g. team meetings, work reviews) and associating it with the joke from a month ago
special_situations.conditional_assumptions: If my supervisor once mocked or noticed my inadequacy, it means she thinks I am incompetent and may act against me at any time
special_situations.compensatory_strategies: Avoiding contact with the supervisor and colleagues, trying to prove worth but not daring to seek feedback directly
special_situations.automatic_thoughts: She must think I am no good, I may lose my job

special_situations.event: When facing seemingly simple daily tasks, nervous for fear of making mistakes
special_situations.conditional_assumptions: Tasks must be done perfectly, otherwise it proves my incompetence
special_situations.compensatory_strategies: Procrastinating or over-preparing, repeatedly confirming to avoid any mistakes
special_situations.automatic_thoughts: If anything is not done well, everything is lost

core_conflict.wish: Desiring to be recognized as competent and to obtain stable, safe relationships and evaluations
core_conflict.fear: Fearing being seen as incompetent and thus rejected/losing the job, and letting students fail so that self-worth is negated
defense_goal: Lowering the risk of being negated by avoiding authority situations and self-reproach
Temporarily relieving anxiety through excessive control and perfectionist standards

object_relations.self_representation: Prone to mistakes, needing constant self-justification, a 'problem employee/teacher'
object_relations.object_representation: A picky superior/authority prone to humiliating and negating people

object_relations.self_representation: A teacher fully responsible for students, who must teach everything well
object_relations.object_representation: A vulnerable student group highly dependent on their own success or failure

manifestations: The heaviness of 'responsibility-choice': attributing students' academic success or failure entirely to their own responsibility
Fearing negation in front of superiors, longing for external recognition and security

contact_model.definition: The individual takes in external rules and expectations without digesting them, treating them as their own standards or absolute truths, corresponding to 'rejection'. Language manifestations include: 'I must/should...', 'Everyone is like this', and so on.
manifestations: Emphasizing 'I must be responsible for students' academics', equating student success or failure with self-worth
Evaluates own performance by perfectionistic standards, with an extremely low tolerance for error

contact_model.definition: The individual ignores or avoids a stimulus from the internal or external environment, deliberately avoiding direct contact, corresponding to 'acceptance'. Language manifestations include: 'Speaking of which... haha, just kidding', 'In theory...', and so on
manifestations: Avoids direct contact with supervisors and colleagues, reducing communication
Trying to avoid conversations before and after review or meeting situations to dodge anxiety triggers

contact_model.definition: The individual has a poor capacity for self-reflection and introspection, with excessive self-restriction and self-blame, and is overly cautious about contact, corresponding to 'autonomy'. Language manifestations include: 'It is all my fault that he was hurt', 'I do not deserve to talk to him', and so on
manifestations: Persistent self-doubt and self-blame, worrying that one mistake proves incompetence
Overly cautious about work details, checks repeatedly, hard to relax

positive_force: Has a supportive spouse, can confide emotionally
Having previously good task-organization ability (used to be good at arranging daily work)
Proactively seeks professional help and is willing to set small, feasible goals
Having tried multiple strategies and extra support in teaching to help students
negative_force: Catastrophizing, overgeneralization, and all-or-nothing thinking patterns reinforce helplessness
Excessive responsibility attribution and high dependence on external evaluation (seeks external validation)
Avoiding interaction with authorities and colleagues, leading to maintained anxiety and declining function
Persistent worry leads to sleep and diet disturbance, lowering recovery and focus

target_behavior.behavior: Work-related persistent anxiety and negative anticipation (worrying about student failure/being seen as incompetent by the supervisor)
antecedent: During classroom teaching and lesson preparation
When the boss is present, team meetings, or work reviews
target_behavior.core_reason: Completely equating student success or failure with self-worth, and interpreting the supervisor's joke and attention as negation of their own ability, accompanied by catastrophizing and 'all-or-nothing' beliefs
target_behavior.function: Gaining a sense of control in the short term through excessive worry and self-monitoring, avoiding the risk of being evaluated
target_behavior.consequence: Teaching and decreased work efficiency, anxiety maintained and worsened, sleep and diet disturbance, interpersonal tension

target_behavior.behavior: Avoiding contact with supervisors and colleagues
antecedent: Before and after team meetings or work reviews
When recalling the boss's joke about 'one-handed typing'
target_behavior.core_reason: Fearing negation and being seen as incompetent, over-interpreting external signals as threats
target_behavior.function: Avoiding unwelcome evaluation situations to quickly lower anxiety
target_behavior.consequence: Workplace interaction impaired, support and feedback reduced, anxiety and insecurity maintained

target_behavior.behavior: Sleep difficulties and disordered eating (overeating or forgetting to eat)
antecedent: Recalling daytime worries and mistakes at night on workdays
When there is a task or meeting involving the supervisor the next day
target_behavior.core_reason: High-level physiological arousal driven by persistent worry; negative automatic thoughts are hard to interrupt
target_behavior.function: Non-functional (symptomatic reaction), mutually reinforcing with anxiety
target_behavior.consequence: Energy declines, attention and executive function are impaired, further affecting teaching and work performance
